chunks.title: What Are Proposal Custom Pages
chunks.content: Proposal custom pages are self-contained HTML blocks that render inside viewProposal.jsp. Each block sits inside a <div class="proposal-section custom-section"> container, on a #f8f9fa light gray background, within a max-width: 900px centered container. Each custom page is a standalone HTML fragment with its own <style> block. The server renders the HTML unescaped, so whatever you generate appears exactly as written. There are 4 default section types (TITLE, FEATURES, PRICING, CLOSING) plus unlimited CUSTOM pages. TITLE, CLOSING, and CUSTOM sections accept raw HTML with <style> blocks and merge tokens.

chunks.title: The Rendering Context
chunks.content: The proposal viewer (viewProposal.jsp) uses Bootstrap 5. The page background is #f8f9fa, the main container is max-width: 900px centered. Each section renders inside <div class="proposal-section">. The server sanitizes HTML before storing it: it strips <script> tags entirely, removes all on* event handlers (onclick, onload, onerror, etc.), and removes javascript: protocol links. However, <style> blocks are intentionally preserved — this is how we deliver CSS for styled pages. Never use <script>, event handlers, or javascript: links in your output.

chunks.title: Merge Tokens Available
chunks.content:
The following merge tokens are replaced server-side with real values before rendering:

{{PROSPECT_NAME}} — Company or prospect name
{{AGENT_NAME}} — Sales agent's full name
{{AGENT_EMAIL}} — Sales agent's email address
{{AGENCY_NAME}} — Agency name
{{PSP_NAME}} — PSP company full name
{{DATE_CREATED}} — Proposal creation date (formatted as 'March 10, 2026')
{{PRIMARY_COLOR}} — PSP brand primary color (hex value like #2B5F8A)
{{ACCENT_COLOR}} — PSP brand accent color (hex value like #7AB648)
{{APPLY_BUTTON}} — Renders a fully styled Apply Now button with link
{{PROPOSAL_ID}} — The proposal's database ID

{{PRIMARY_COLOR}} and {{ACCENT_COLOR}} can be used inside CSS custom properties to make pages automatically brand-adaptive. Example: --primary: {{PRIMARY_COLOR}}; --accent: {{ACCENT_COLOR}};

chunks.title: The Card-Inset Pattern
CSS Scoping Rules
chunks.content:
Every CSS selector must start with the unique prefix class to prevent collisions with Bootstrap and other proposal sections. Pick a short, unique prefix per block — examples: .cobra1, .fsa3, .about2, .title1, .close1.

CRITICAL: Do NOT use Bootstrap class names as your own class names — even when scoped. The viewer loads Bootstrap 5 which applies base styles to .card, .btn, .container, .row, .col, etc. Using these names causes style bleed (e.g., Bootstrap .card sets background-color:#fff and border which override your dark backgrounds). Use unique names: .tile, .info-box, .panel, .block, .service-tile, etc.

Example of proper scoping:
.cobra1 h1 { ... }  /* Good — scoped */
.cobra1 .tile { ... }  /* Good — unique name */
h1 { ... }  /* BAD — affects entire page */
.cobra1 .card { ... }  /* BAD — Bootstrap .card base styles still apply */
.card { ... }  /* BAD — collides with Bootstrap */

chunks.title: The Scale Factor --s
chunks.content:
Define --s:1 on the prefix class. Every font-size, padding, margin, gap, and icon dimension uses calc(value * var(--s)). This lets the user scale the entire page proportionally by changing one number.

Example: --s:1.05 scales everything up 5%, --s:0.95 shrinks 5%.

What to scale with var(--s): font-size, padding, margin, gap, icon width/height.
What NOT to scale: min-height (physical page dimension), border-radius (aesthetic), unitless line-height multipliers, border-top accent widths.

Example usage:
.prefix h1 { font-size: calc(24pt * var(--s)); margin: 0 0 calc(0.5rem * var(--s)) 0; }
.prefix .body { font-size: calc(11pt * var(--s)); line-height: 1.6; }

chunks.title: Responsive Rules
Style Adaptation from Source Material
chunks.content:
CRITICAL: When the user provides reference content (a description, a brochure URL, existing HTML, or style direction), you must analyze the source's visual language BEFORE generating any CSS.

Identify these elements from the source:
- Background color preference (light vs dark vs colored)
- Font family and weight distribution
- Heading scale and hierarchy
- Color palette (extract actual hex values where possible)
- Icon style (outlined vs filled, round vs square containers)
- Card/box shapes (border-radius, shadows, borders vs fills)
- Spacing density (airy vs compact)
- Whether accent colors appear as backgrounds, borders, or text

The card-inset is the STRUCTURAL foundation, but its background, color, font-family, border-radius, and accent colors should ALL adapt to match the user's intent.

The default dark navy palette (#1B2A4A with teal #2A7F8E accents) is a FALLBACK — not mandatory. If the user wants white/light, use white. If they want corporate blue, use corporate blue. If they provide a Gamma deck with pink accents, use pink accents.

chunks.title: Color Palette Customization
chunks.content:
The default palette works for generic pages: navy #1B2A4A, lighter navy #243B5C, teal #2A7F8E, teal background #1E5F6B. But the AI should ask about or detect the desired color scheme.

Using merge tokens for brand-adaptive styling:
--primary: {{PRIMARY_COLOR}};
--accent: {{ACCENT_COLOR}};

This makes pages automatically match any PSP's configured brand colors without hardcoding.

When to hardcode colors:
- User specifies exact hex values
- Creating a one-off design with specific colors
- User wants a universal look regardless of PSP brand

When to use merge tokens:
- User says 'use our brand colors' or 'match our branding'
- Creating reusable templates that work across multiple PSPs
- User wants the page to auto-adapt to their configured colors

chunks.title: Font Selection
chunks.content:
Default font is Source Sans 3 via @import inside the <style> block. The AI can suggest different fonts based on content type:

Professional/corporate: Inter, Lato, Source Sans 3
Elegant/upscale: Playfair Display (headings) + Source Sans 3 (body)
Modern/clean: DM Sans (matches the main AMS UI)
Friendly/approachable: DM Sans, Nunito

Always use @import inside the <style> block for Google Fonts. Never use <link> tags — they won't work reliably in the proposal viewer.

Example: @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;600;700&display=swap');

chunks.title: Two-Column Info Boxes Layout
Card Grid Layout (2x2 or 3-col)
Stat Rings / Metrics Layout
Callout Box Layout
Full-Page Size Budget
chunks.content:
Target card-inset height: 912px (9.5 inches at 96dpi, from 11in page minus 1.5in padding).

Page budget math:
- Total card height: ~912px
- Card padding top+bottom: ~76px → ~836px usable
- Title + subtitle: ~60-80px
- Body paragraph: ~40-60px
- Remaining: ~700px for info boxes, grids, stats, callouts

Text-heavy content → use smaller fonts (9-10pt body, 8.5pt bullets)
Sparse content → use larger fonts (11-12pt body, 19-20pt subtitle)

Put flex:1 on one expandable section so it stretches to fill remaining space. Use align-content:center on grid layouts so content centers vertically within the flex area.

chunks.title: Title Page Design
Closing Page Design
chunks.content:
The CLOSING section wraps up the proposal with a call to action. It should include:
- CTA language encouraging the prospect to apply
- {{APPLY_BUTTON}} token which renders a styled Apply Now button with the correct link
- Agent contact info via {{AGENT_NAME}}, {{AGENT_EMAIL}} tokens
- Optionally: disclaimers, next-steps timeline, or a brief 'what happens next' section

The APPLY_BUTTON token renders a full <a> element with inline styling, so just place it where you want the button to appear. The button uses the PSP's accent color automatically.

chunks.title: Custom Page Design
chunks.content:
CUSTOM sections appear between FEATURES/PRICING and CLOSING. Common uses:
- 'About Us' company overview page
- Specific benefit line explanations (COBRA administration, FSA/HSA, ICHRA, Transit/Parking)
- Compliance highlights and regulatory overview
- Case studies or testimonials
- Team bios or contact directory
- Service process timeline (how onboarding works)

Each custom page is completely standalone — it has its own <style> block and scoped prefix. Multiple custom pages can be added to a single proposal, and each can have different styling if desired.

Custom pages support scope filtering: they can be set to show on ALL proposals or only when specific Lines of Service or Enhancements are included in the proposal.

chunks.title: Example: Dark Navy About Us Page
chunks.content:
A dark navy About Us page with teal accents uses the default palette. Structure:
- Title: 'About {{PSP_NAME}}' at 24pt
- Subtitle: company tagline at 14pt
- Body paragraph: brief company description at 10.5pt
- 2x2 card grid with icon circles: each card has a teal icon, heading, and description
- Callout box at bottom: key differentiator or quote
- Stats row (optional): 3-4 stat rings showing years in business, clients served, etc.

The .grid section gets flex:1 to fill remaining vertical space. Cards use border-top: 3px solid var(--teal) for accent. Icon circles use background: rgba(42,127,142,0.2) with teal text color.

chunks.title: Building a Page Step by Step
chunks.content:
The question-based workflow for building a proposal page:

1. What is this page about? (About Us, COBRA overview, FSA details, title page, closing page, etc.)
2. What section type? (TITLE for cover page, CLOSING for final page, CUSTOM for everything else)
3. What style/color scheme? (dark navy default, light/white, specific brand colors, match a reference)
4. What content to include? (specific text, bullet points, stats, team info, etc.)
5. Any merge tokens needed? (prospect name, agent info, brand colors, apply button)

Then generate the HTML block following the card-inset skeleton, apply the chosen style, fill with content, and output in a code block.

After generating, explain what you built and offer to adjust colors, font sizes, layout, or content.

chunks.title: Font Sizing Guide
chunks.content:
Calibrated font sizes for the 900px container. Pick sizes based on content density:

- Page title: 22-26pt, weight 700
- Subtitle: 19-20pt, weight 700, slightly muted color
- Section heading: 12-13pt, weight 700
- Body text: 10-12pt, line-height 1.5-1.7
- Info box text: 10-10.5pt, line-height 1.55
- Card body text: 9-10pt, line-height 1.4-1.5
- Bullet items: 8.5-9.5pt, line-height 1.35-1.45
- Callout text: 9.5-10.5pt
- Badges/tags: 7-8pt

All font sizes should use calc(Xpt * var(--s)) for the scale factor. Text-heavy pages should use sizes at the lower end of each range.
